landmarks.name: L'Auberge Symmes (Symmes Inn)
landmarks.arriving: A commanding 1831 heritage stone building terminating the visual axis of Rue Principale right where the street meets the Ottawa River and Parc des Cèdres, flanked by mature conifer trees and the waterfront promenade.
landmarks.structure: 2.5-storey rectangular Georgian/vernacular stone building with coursed limestone ashlar masonry, large corner quoins, medium-pitch side-gable roof, two tall cut-stone chimneys rising at the gable ends, an exterior wooden staircase on the gable end, and a symmetrical 5-bay fenestration pattern with 12-pane (6-over-6) sash windows and dark shutters.
landmarks.materials: Coursed grey limestone ashlar blocks with mortar joints, stone lintels and sills, sheet metal/standing seam gabled roof, painted wood window sashes, shutters, exterior wooden stair/balcony, and panelled wooden entry door.
landmarks.colours: Weathered light grey and beige limestone masonry, dark forest green roof, shutters, doors, and trim; white window sashes.
landmarks.groundSurfaces: Smooth asphalt roadway (Rue Principale/Rue Front) ending at the park turnaround; red/buff brick-paver sidewalk along the street edge; gravel driveway apron; mown green turf lawn surrounding the building; shoreline rip-rap boulders along the riverbank.
recognisable: Massive 1831 Georgian cut-limestone ashlar facade with distinct corner quoins and symmetrical 5-bay window rhythm
Twin tall stone chimneys at opposite gable ends and steep green gabled roof with exterior timber fire escape stair
Scenic waterfront park setting at the foot of Rue Principale overlooking Lac Deschênes (Ottawa River)
landmarks.changedSince: Ongoing museum preservation maintenance, landscape enhancements, interpretive signage updates, and historical plaque installations.
inferred: Interior structural timber framing and basement cellar masonry

landmarks.name: Les Galeries d'Aylmer
landmarks.arriving: A vast sea of asphalt parking stretching horizontally in front of a sprawling low-profile single-storey suburban enclosed shopping mall, punctuated by tall illuminated pylon signage and distinct retail anchor facades.
landmarks.structure: Single-storey horizontal commercial complex with varying parapet heights for anchor boxes (Canadian Tire, Zellers, Cinema, SAQ), glass-and-steel entrance vestibules with projecting canopies, and service bays along the rear/side perimeters.
landmarks.materials: Precast concrete panels, fluted concrete block, brick masonry accents, steel-framed glass storefronts, flat commercial membrane roof, painted metal fascia bands, and tubular steel light poles.
landmarks.colours: Beige and light grey concrete block walls, bright red Canadian Tire fascia, vintage red Zellers lettering and signage, white and blue cinema/transit pylon signage, dark asphalt pavement.
landmarks.groundSurfaces: Multi-lane asphalt boulevard (Rue Principale/Chemin d'Aylmer) bordered by concrete curbs and red-brick accent sidewalks; massive asphalt parking lot with painted yellow/white parking stalls and driving lanes; grass swale/berm with low ornamental shrubs separating the lot from the roadway.
recognisable: Vast open asphalt surface parking lot with tall high-mast floodlight standards fronting the long horizontal mall facade
Prominent roadside pylon sign near the main road entrance announcing Cinema, Billard, Terminus, and SAQ Classique
Classic vintage 2000s retail anchor branding, notably the prominent red Zellers store and Canadian Tire
landmarks.changedSince: Zellers anchor replaced following chain closure; exterior facade reclad/modernized in sections; updated mall tenant branding and entrance renovations.
inferred: Internal enclosed mall concourse layout and structural steel roof spans

landmarks.name: Aylmer Marina & Plage des Cèdres
landmarks.arriving: A sweeping expanse of the Ottawa River / Lac Deschênes framed by mature cedar trees, a long curved stone breakwater sheltering hundreds of boat slips, a clubhouse/capitainerie, paved boat launch ramp, and sandy public beach.
landmarks.structure: Long curved rock-armoured rip-rap breakwater jetty extending into the bay with a navigation light beacon at its head; wooden/aluminium floating dock pontoons arranged in finger slips; 1.5-storey wood/siding capitainerie clubhouse; concrete multi-lane boat launch ramp; open crescent sand beach with lifeguard stands.
landmarks.materials: Granite/limestone rock boulder armouring on breakwater, treated wood and aluminium floating dock systems, wood and vinyl siding on clubhouse/service pavilions, concrete boat ramp slabs, steel security gates, wooden picnic tables.
landmarks.colours: Grey and charcoal rock boulders, natural weathered grey wood decking, white and dark green boat club buildings, golden-brown sand beach, deep green lawn and cedar groves.
landmarks.groundSurfaces: Asphalt approach roads and designated parking areas (main marina lot and beach lot) with concrete curbs; packed gravel boat trailer staging areas; wide sandy beach along the shoreline; manicured grass turf parkland throughout Parc des Cèdres with paved multi-use asphalt bicycle paths.
recognisable: Curved stone rip-rap breakwater extending into Lac Deschênes sheltering the marina docks and boat slips
Wide crescent-shaped sandy public beach flanked by expansive grassy parkland and mature cedar trees (Parc des Cèdres)
Dedicated multi-lane concrete boat launch ramp with adjacent paved trailer parking area
landmarks.changedSince: Upgrades to floating dock infrastructure, shoreline stabilization work, rebuilt park pavilion facilities, and modernized beach amenities.
inferred: Submerged bathymetry around dock slips and breakwater base

landmarks.name: Champlain Bridge (Pont Champlain - Québec Side & Bate Island)
landmarks.arriving: A wide multi-lane bridge structure carrying traffic across the rapids of the Ottawa River toward Ottawa, framed by overhead gantries with electronic lane control signals and sweeping views of the river and forested Bate Island midway across.
landmarks.structure: Multi-span prestressed concrete girder bridge supported by rounded concrete piers anchored into the rocky riverbed; 3 vehicular travel lanes (including a reversible centre lane controlled by overhead gantry signals); raised concrete sidewalk / multi-use cycling path on the western (upstream) edge; continuous steel tubular railing and concrete crash barriers.
landmarks.materials: Reinforced and prestressed concrete deck, concrete piers and abutments, steel overhead signal gantry truss, painted white/grey steel tubular bridge parapet railings, asphalt deck wearing course.
landmarks.colours: Light grey concrete structure, dark asphalt roadway, yellow and white painted lane markings, white/grey railings, silver steel overhead gantry with black electronic signal boxes showing green arrows and red X marks.
landmarks.groundSurfaces: Smooth dark asphalt road surface across the entire bridge deck and approach roads; concrete curbs and raised pedestrian/bike walkway; on Bate Island: asphalt loop road, gravel parking shoulders and turnouts, natural grass picnic meadows, and exposed rocky river shorelines.
recognisable: Overhead steel gantry with electronic reversible lane control signals (illuminated green arrows, red X, and HOV diamond icons)
Multi-span low-profile concrete girder bridge crossing over the rapids to Bate Island and the Ontario shore
Forested Bate Island midway across the bridge with gravel park pull-offs, mature pines, and rapids access
landmarks.changedSince: Complete deck reconstruction and widening in recent years to add a dedicated bidirectional active transportation path with high architectural safety barriers; updated electronic lane gantries.
inferred: Sub-surface pier foundation depth into bedrock
